messages:
Alex (PM): quick sync — putting together a launch checklist + priorities for VPC control plane + on-prem packaging. need to call out air-gap constraints, legal must-haves, and what we commit for the next quarter. thoughts?
Sam (Eng): MVP proposal: 1) VPC control plane (customer VPC, our control plane components run in their VPC) 2) on-prem installer (k8s helm + operator) 3) air-gapped option later (offline bundle + install script). keep it iterative. :+1:
Anne (Infra): important to nail network model up front. do we require customer-managed NAT/proxy for outbound, or do we allow optional egress? fully air-gapped means no TLS callbacks to our control plane.
Maya (Sales): customers keep asking for rpm/apt installers and support for RHEL/CentOS and AKS/eks-distro. biggest deals want "no internet by default" but are ok with controlled egress.
Bob (Legal): data residency + export-control checklist: KMS integration, no telemetry by default for air-gapped, and add SOC2 + DPA language for Private. will need to review redistributable model licenses if we include weights in the installer.
Tina (Solutions): proposed prioritization: 1) VPC control plane (shortest path to revenue) 2) online on-prem installer (works behind proxy) 3) fully air-gapped packaging (special case). can we run 1 & 2 in parallel?
Sam (Eng): we can parallelize some work but runtime/inference changes and packaging infra are blocking for on-prem. rough estimates: control plane core work ~6w, on-prem installer baseline ~8w, air-gap packaging + compliance ~+4w. depends on how much QA we add.
Alex (PM): OKR alignment note — Q3 pledge: ship VPC control plane + on-prem POC. air-gapped is Q4 target unless we get a strategic customer commit to accelerate. is everyone aligned?
Anne (Infra): also need e2e upgrade/rollback runbook, automated smoke tests, and k8s support matrix (1.22-1.25 to start). and cluster bootstrap docs for SRE.
Bob (Legal): SLA/consequence: for Private deployments we should offer support packages (bronze/silver/gold) — legal prefers documented responsibilities matrix (we operate control plane vs customer operates).
Maya (Sales): qualifying question for customers: do they require model weights inside the bundle? that's the main blocker for air-gapped installs. many are OK with separate secure transfer of weights.
Sam (Eng): technical note: offline bundle size will be large if weights included (~3GB+). alternative: lightweight runtime + weights served from local registry the customer seeds. also need to define upgrade mechanism for offline.
Tina (Solutions): action items (suggested):
- Alex: draft launch criteria and checklist (what counts as "launched")
- Sam/Anne: high-level implementation plan + timelines + key tech risks
- Bob: list mandatory compliance artifacts and any license blockers
- Maya: top-3 customer POC candidates and their must-haves
- Tina: create internal demo plan and security review checklist
deploy-bot: created doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/private-deploy/checklist (permissions: product, eng)
Alex (PM): I'll draft the initial checklist by EOD and schedule a 30-min triage tomorrow 11am PT. please add items to the doc and drop blockers here. :eyes:
Sam (Eng): added risk note about model licensing to the doc.
Anne (Infra): added k8s matrix and test plan.
Maya (Sales): pinging for customer availability for POCs next week.
Bob (Legal): will upload DPA template and KMS integration checklist by EOD.
Tina (Solutions): +1, thanks.
Alex (PM): ok great — agree on VPC first, on-prem baseline second, air-gap as opt-in. closing with :thumbsup: — see you tomorrow.
